title: Finite affine component subatlases of quasi-compact point spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and give $|Z|$ its field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose $|Z|$ is quasi-compact, meaning that every open covering has a finite subcover. For any representable surjective etale atlas $p:h_U\to Z$ with $U=\coprod_{d\in D}U_d$ a set-indexed disjoint union of affine $S$-schemes, there is a finite subset $D_0\subseteq D$ such that the open subscheme $U'=\coprod_{d\in D_0}U_d\subseteq U$ is quasi-compact and $p|_{U'}:h_{U'}\to Z$ is representable surjective etale. Open subschemes use [def-weil-open-immersion]; the coproduct has its usual scheme topology, in which its summands are pairwise disjoint open subschemes covering $U$. This includes $Z=\varnothing$, when $D_0=\varnothing$ is permitted and $U'$ is the empty quasi-compact scheme. Independently, for any continuous morphism on point spaces $|B|\to|C|$ induced by a morphism of algebraic spaces $B\to C$, if it is surjective and $|B|$ is quasi-compact, then $|C|$ is quasi-compact. In particular any representable surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme has quasi-compact target point space.

proof.text: For the given atlas p, use lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover to identify the existing final point topology with the atlas topology and obtain that schemePointMap p is open. Scheme-test surjectivity gives surjectivity of schemePointMap p directly: test on a field-valued representative, choose a point of the surjective scheme test, and use its residue field to compare classes. Residue-field functoriality proves schemePointMap (yoneda.map i ≫ p) = schemePointMap p ∘ i on ordinary scheme points.

proof.text: The images schemePointMap p (V d) are open and cover |Z|, since p is point-surjective and the given opens cover U. Apply Mathlib IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover to the compact whole point space. Let D₀ be the resulting finite set and W the open supremum of V d for d in D₀. Every point class has a preimage in W by the finite-subcover inclusion.

proof.text: The finite union W is compact: each V d is compact by lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs, and Mathlib Set.Finite.isCompact_biUnion proves compactness of their finite union. The carrier of W.toScheme is that subtype. This works for an empty chosen set without a nonemptiness assumption; disjointness is not needed for compactness of a finite union.

proof.text: The inclusion W.ι is an open immersion and hence etale. Scheme pullbacks and Yoneda transport show that yoneda.map of an etale scheme morphism is representable etale; compose with p using isEtale_comp. Regard W.toScheme over S as its existing representable algebraic space using def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space. The representable point-surjectivity criterion in lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus then turns the point-surjectivity from the finite subcover into IsSurjective for the restricted map. A scheme point y supplies the class of its residue field in h_W, so the ordinary scheme-source surjectivity suffices for that criterion.

proof.text: For the independent continuous-surjection assertion, install the given CompactSpace instance and apply Mathlib Function.Surjective.compactSpace, the range-image specialization of lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact. For a scheme atlas, continuity follows directly from its term in the supremum defining pointTopologicalSpace; the residue-field argument of step 1 supplies surjectivity. Apply the same Mathlib theorem to the compact scheme. No algebraic-space compactness instance on the representable point classes is needed.
